findings.detail: 'type' can be NULL, and it is passed as argument 0 to type_clear_flags(), which dereferences that parameter at line 478 with no NULL guard of its own. **Control dies here**, not at any later sink in this function -- a rule that only looks at sinks written in this body reports a line the crash never reaches. Guard 'type' before the call, or add the guard to type_clear_flags().

'type' can be NULL and sits at argument 1 of PyObject_CallFunctionObjArgs(), whose argument list is terminated by the first NULL. A NULL here does not crash and does not raise: the call silently becomes a 0-argument call and obj is dropped. A different function is invoked than the one written, so this is a wrong-behaviour (CONSIDER) finding rather than a crash. Guard the field, or pass it positionally through a non-sentinel API.

'type' can be NULL, and it is passed as argument 0 to supercheck(), which dereferences that parameter at line 12763 with no NULL guard of its own. **Control dies here**, not at any later sink in this function -- a rule that only looks at sinks written in this body reports a line the crash never reaches. Guard 'type' before the call, or add the guard to supercheck(). Control dies here: the sink(s) at :12806 are downstream on the same path and are never reached.

'type' is Py_INCREF'd via Py_NewRef() with no NULL guard, but it can be NULL via a __new__/subclass bypass of tp_init (T.__new__(T) leaves it NULL). A guard such as 'type != Py_None' or 'Py_IsNone(type)' does NOT protect this — after the bypass the field is NULL. Add 'if (type == NULL)' (or initialize it in tp_new) before the deref. NOTE: unreachable when the field is NULL -- the sink at :12797 on the same path already crashes. Cite that line, not this one.
